_comment: OCI-to-SIF provenance for the reference container image (recorded 2026-09-08; refreshed 2026-09-12 when the image was rebuilt to bake in the NLTK punkt_tab tokenizer). The image was built by the hardened build-sif-image CI workflow from an immutable source commit, pushed to the GitHub Container Registry by digest, and converted to an Apptainer SIF on a Linux compute node from that exact digest. The workflow's provenance artifact could not be uploaded (artifact-storage quota), so the values below were taken from the build-provenance JSON the workflow printed to its build log and re-checked here: every recipe hash against `git show <source_commit>:<path>`, and the SIF hash with sha256sum on the compute node that built it. certification/EXPECTED_SIF_SHA carries the same SIF hash.
status_note: This image implements the R 4.1.3 + fixest 0.10.4 recipe that environment_decision below selects. The condition attached to that decision -- a full real-data run inside this exact image -- was met on 2026-09-14 (source commit 84f53b7); the hash-bound certification run of the final deposit archive on the real data is still pending.

recipe.renv_lock_note: The build logged renv_lock_sha256 = MISSING because the workflow at the source commit hashed a top-level renv.lock that does not exist. The value recorded here is the SHA-256 of docker/renv.lock at the source commit. The workflow's provenance step was corrected for later builds.
recipe.build_workflow_note: The SHA-256 of the build workflow file as it ran, at the source commit. A later commit changed only its provenance step (the renv.lock path and a non-fatal artifact upload), not the image build itself.

base_image.note: Resolved and pinned by digest by the workflow at build time (--build-arg BASE_REF).

oci_image.ci_verify_output: pdflatex: pdfTeX 3.14159265-2.6-1.40.20 (TeX Live 2019/Debian) | numpy 1.26.4 | nltk corpora OK. The docker build itself printed: NLTK corpora verified: punkt, punkt_tab, stopwords, wordnet, omw-1.4; word_tokenize works offline.
oci_image.conversion_command: apptainer build fda_np126_a0f2fac.sif docker://ghcr.io/parkerrogers/fda-np126@sha256:e779c623f83347abf0d5b4b078d61b4166b6a8a67593ba19676acfb43c5c7869 (run on a Linux compute node; a read-only registry token was supplied on stdin; the result was then installed under the name fda_np126.sif)

sif.verification: Verified on a Linux compute node on 2026-09-12 with `apptainer exec --cleanenv --containall --net none`: nltk 3.9.2 with punkt_tab present at /opt/nltk_data/tokenizers/punkt_tab/english and word_tokenize working with no network; numpy 1.26.4, pandas 2.3.3, rpy2 3.6.4, R 4.1.3, fixest 0.10.4, data.table 1.14.2. A full file-level comparison against the superseded image below found: identical package versions (790 dpkg packages, 190 pip packages, 203 R packages); byte-identical fixest, data.table, numpy, pandas, scipy and torch binaries; the NLTK punkt_tab tokenizer newly present under /opt/nltk_data (78 files); 23 R packages (including didimputation), rpy2 and the source-built Python recompiled during the image build and therefore differing byte-wise; and differences in Python bytecode caches, TeX and font caches, build logs, /etc/group, the image labels, and two comment lines of docker/entrypoint.sh.
sif.superseded_note: An earlier interim image, built by CI from docker/Dockerfile on a feature branch, in which the NLTK punkt_tab tokenizer was missing. Its hash is recorded here only so that it cannot be mistaken for the reference image's; it is not the reference image and must not be used.

in_image_expected_current_recipe.nltk: 3.9.2 (punkt, punkt_tab, stopwords, wordnet, omw-1.4 baked into /opt/nltk_data)
in_image_expected_current_recipe.preflight: before running anything, the certification script checks the SIF's sha256 against certification/EXPECTED_SIF_SHA and records the in-image numpy and pdflatex versions
in_image_expected_current_recipe.note: these are the versions the committed docker/Dockerfile and docker/renv.lock pin; per environment_decision below, this is the selected recipe

environment_decision.decided: 2026-09-12 (author), made conditional on 2026-09-14 (author): KEEP R 4.1.3 + fixest 0.10.4 (with numpy 1.26.4) as the selected environment, conditional on a full real-data comparison inside this exact image reproducing the manuscript. Had it not, the R 4.0.1 + fixest 0.12.1 option would have reopened. This supersedes the 2026-09-08 decision recorded below, which was to rebuild on R 4.0.1 + fixest 0.12.1 if the then-current container did not reproduce the manuscript.
environment_decision.pending_evidence: What remains is the hash-bound certification run of the final deposit archive on the real data. Already done, on 2026-09-14 (source commit 84f53b7): a full real-data run in this exact image (SIF b9f9ee2a) starting from empty outputs, which completed run_all with 25 steps run, 0 failed and 11 skipped; all 50 formatted tables byte-identical to the committed copies; the strict numeric comparator matching 120 of 130 files, with the remaining 10 event-study CSVs agreeing to within 4.44e-14 (numerical equivalence); the semantic comparator passing; and the in-text number gate passing on all 38 scalars it then covered. The other evidence listed below predates this image.
evidence: 2026-09-12, on the superseded image above (whose package versions are identical to this image, but whose source-built libraries, including didimputation and rpy2, were recompiled for it): 03a_estimation_3to2.py on the real data reproduced all 50 committed tables byte-for-byte under fixest 0.10.4 and under 0.12.1, under the OpenBLAS Zen, Haswell, SandyBridge, Nehalem and Prescott kernels, and under the reference BLAS.

2026-09-05, on an earlier build of the same R 4.1.3 recipe with the Python pipeline run by a separate numpy 1.26.4 environment: a forced full-estimation real-data run starting from the derived data (the generation steps did not run) regenerated all 50 output/tables/Formatted/*.tex byte-identically. Of 140 committed output/tables CSVs, 123 were byte-identical, 15 differed only in the last floating-point digits (maximum absolute difference 7.2e-14, from full-precision intermediates), and 2 differed only because the committed copies predated later code changes.

The 0.1-0.6 % (one 3.6 %) differences cited under the superseded decision came from a June 2026 Docker run under x86_64 emulation on an Apple-silicon Mac. They did not replicate on native Linux, and their cause was not identified; the tests above rule out both the BLAS kernel and the fixest version.

All of the tests above ran on AMD EPYC 7742 Linux nodes. The hash-bound real-data certification run of the final deposit archive in this image is the definitive check; the full real-data run in this image from empty outputs, recorded under pending_evidence, is the interim check.

superseded_2026_09_08.decided: 2026-09-08 (author): LOCK the reference image on the environment in which the manuscript's R-estimated numbers were produced -- R 4.0.1 + fixest 0.12.1, with numpy 1.26.4 -- so that the container reproduces them directly, conditional on the rebuilt container actually reproducing them.

fallback.note: the committed docker/Dockerfile, docker/renv.lock and requirements-lock.txt pin this fallback and are retained; taking the fallback route, with its 0.1-0.6 % cross-environment R/fixest differences, would have required the Data Editor's written acceptance of a semantic rather than byte-identical comparison of the real-data outputs

superseded_2026_09_08.historical_action_not_taken: Rebuilding off-cluster at the target R 4.0.1 / fixest 0.12.1 (regenerating renv.lock for R 4.0.1), verifying that it reproduces the manuscript numbers, then refreshing this file's recipe hashes and digests together with certification/EXPECTED_SIF_SHA, and falling back to R 4.1.3 plus the Data Editor's acceptance of a semantic comparison only if the R 4.0.1 container did not reproduce across platforms. The recipe was not changed, because that rebuild could not be built or tested off-cluster.
